newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.S. Gov wants Conrail pact to boost economy.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.S. Gov wants Conrail pact to boost economy.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki on Thursday said he would try to capitalize on a plan reached by two railroads to split a freight carrier, Conrail, to ensure the $10.3 billion deal boosts the state's economy.

CSX Corp and Norfolk Southern Corp earlier this week unveiled the details of their plan to split key routes of the Philadelphia-based freight carrier. Pataki noted Conrail runs more than 2,000 miles of track in New York State, serves all its major cities and is the only interstate rail carrier serving the New York City market.

Noting that the Port of New York and New Jersey's future as the most important port on the East Coast depends in part on its inland connections to move goods, Pataki said: "In addition, the economies and businesses of upstate areas rely upon freight access to receive and deliver products at competitive price to New York's residents. Therefore, any merger must result in improved services and competitive prices for freight movement in New York State."
Pataki listed a number of ambitious objectives for the merger, detailed in the following list, that the state Department of Transportation (DOT) produced after holding hearings.
"These objectives will guide the DOT as it develops the state's position on the rail merger plan," the release added.
--Raising employment in New York due to more freight shipments and lower prices for companies.
--Accommodating commuter passenger services and growth efforts in the area served by the state Metropolitan Transportation Authority.

--Accommodating Intercity and High Speed Rail passenger services and growth efforts throughout the state, including: New York City to Albany and beyond to Buffalo and Montreal; and New York City to upstate areas west of the Hudson River.
--Restoring competitive rail freight service throughout the state and to the ports of New York and New Jersey thorough separate ownership of the Waterlevel and Southern Tier lines.
--Designating local switching railroads to provide competitive opportunities for connecting with big long-haul and regional railroads at Albany, Buffalo and the ports of New York and New Jersey
--Preserving all existing operating rights and elimination of artificial barriers that act as "fire walls" against open interchange of service for the state's regional and short lines.
--Protecting and raising employment opportunities at the state's railroads.
--Facilitating competitive access to New York City and Long Island from Albany along the east side of the Hudson River.

--Putting in place reciprocal switching for reasonable charge to all carriers at the New York and New Jersey ports and in upstate areas, like Albany, Binghamton, Buffalo, Rochester, Syracuse and Utica.

--Facilitating international economic developement as envisioned in the North American Free Trade Agreement through competitive access to state terminals and ports, including New Jersey ports, by Canadian carriers.
--Creating an "unrestrained opportunity" for carriers to serve local customers along lines for which they have trackage rights.
